articles.title: Our bikes are 'not for jousting,' says Lime after Hackney duel
articles.summary: Footage emerged on social media of hundreds of people gathered in east London to watch a bike joust.
articles.body:
E-bike rental company Lime has said its bikes are "not for jousting" after footage of two riders dressed as knights charging at each other in an east London park circulated over the weekend.

Hundreds of people congregated in London Fields, Hackney, to watch artist Jack Carden and actor Camtholomew the First joust, while riding the bright green rentable e-bikes.

The videos on social media showed them dressed as knights in armour, complete with chainmail and lances, attempting to knock each other off the bikes.

A spokesperson for the company said: "While we appreciate the medieval spirit, safety must always come first."

Ahead of the event, Carden said the "free public joust" was "performance art" in a post on social media.

A video on his Instagram account of the event has been watched more than four million times.

Despite their popularity, hospitals have reported an increase in injuries to both e-bike riders and pedestrians.

A spokesperson for Lime said on Monday: "We always love seeing Londoners come together and build a sense of community in unexpected ways.

"While we appreciate the medieval spirit, safety must always come first.

"Lime bikes are designed for getting around the city, not for jousting.

"We discourage anyone from attempting similar events, to help keep riders and those around them safe."

articles.title: Capybara pups at Manx wildlife park draw record crowds
articles.summary: Curraghs Wildlife Park has its busiest October weekend ever after the birth of eight capybara pups.
articles.body:
Curraghs Wildlife Park has experienced its busiest October weekend ever after the birth of eight capybara pups, which staff say have "delighted" people and boosted conservation funding.

The pups were born to two females within days of each other, on 26 September and 1 October.

Their arrival has sparked huge public interest, with the park's manager Kathleen Graham saying the reaction to this "overload of cuteness" had been extraordinary.

"The car park was full, it was like a bank holiday. Everybody coming to see the capybara babies," she said.

The arrival marks a milestone for the park, which last welcomed a single capybara pup four years ago.

Graham said the scale of this year's births has been "a super overload of cuteness really."

The animals, native to South America, are the world's largest rodent, and thrive in wet marshland environments.

Graham said the pups' appearance on social media immediately drew far more attention than expected, and the surge translated directly into visitor numbers

"They have been delighting people. Even grown men were like cooing," she laughed.

Although capybaras are not endangered, Graham said they play a vital role in helping visitors understand threatened wetland habitats

The park is part of the European Association of Zoos and Aquaria's Eaza Wetlands for Life campaign and sits on a Ramsar‑designated wetland.

Graham said the pups helped highlight how wetlands supported both wildlife and people.

"We rely on wetlands to soak up excess rainwater. And they're management systems, really. So they need looking after and protecting," she said.

The pups' popularity also directly supported conservation work, she explained, as each visitor contributed £1 to the park's conservation fund unless they opted out.

"Although themselves [capybaras] may not be endangered, they've actually created a lot of extra money this weekend for the conservation fund and spread a lot of joy and oohs and aahs," she said.

The fund supports projects locally with Manx Wildlife Trust and internationally, including work in the Pantanal, where wild capybaras live.

She said the pups arrival had lifted spirits at a time when many people were seeking moments of joy.

"I think when there's so many just awful things that happen in the world, sometimes these little things just give us a bit of light relief, don't they?," she added.

articles.title: Waterford arson attack: 'Walk away from drugs' family tells funerals
articles.summary: Parents Philip and Kim English died in the fire alongside their two children, 12-year-old Callum and nine-year-old Jayden.
articles.body:
A relative of four members of the same family who died after a suspected arson attack on a house in Ireland last week has appealed to young people to "walk away from drugs".

Parents Philip and Kim English died in the fire alongside their two children, 12-year-old Callum and nine-year-old Jayden, in their house in the Birchwood estate in Waterford.

The couple's two other children, who were in the house at the time of the fire, are in a critical condition in hospital.

Gardaí (Irish police) believe the arson to be linked to drug debt intimidation, with Philip English's son telling Irish broadcaster RTÉ that they were targeted over someone else's drug debt .

On Saturday, two people appeared in court charged in connection with the attack.

Hundreds of mourners attended the funeral Mass at Sacred Heart Church in the city, with the family buried in Kilbarry Cemetery after the service.

Four coffins, two white and two light brown, stood at the top of the church during the Mass.

A family photo of the six members of the English family, including two children who are critically ill in hospital, stood on a table beside the coffins with four white candles.

Towards the end of the service, Philip's cousin Raymond Power addressed young people "in our city and country".

"Please walk away from drugs," he told the congregation.

"Please ask for help when it comes to addiction. Please ask for help if you're being led down a bad path. Please choose a life, choose hope and please, most certainly, choose a future."

The Mass was led by parish priest Fr Gerry Chestnutt, with aide-de-comps for Irish President Catherine Connolly, Taoiseach (Irish Prime Minister) Micheál Martin and Tanaiste (Irish Deputy Prime Minister) Simon Harris in attendance.

Local politicians, including local TD (member of the Irish parliament) and junior minister John Cummins, as well as leader of Sinn Féin Mary Lou McDonald also attended the funeral.

The gifts brought up to the altar by members of the bereaved family were a Minecraft t-shirt and toys for Jayden, a GAA club jersey for Callum, a Liverpool jersey and Carlsberg beer can for Philip and a bouquet of lilies for Kim.

Fr Chestnutt said the community is "heartbroken" and that the four deceased were the "salt of the earth".

"We are all better people for knowing you, for you were the salt of the earth and lights in this community," he told mourners.

"Last Tuesday morning. an act of total evil left a family and community devastated and heartbroken."

He said "forces of darkness" took four innocent lives and the community is feeling "heartbreak, shock, devastation and, yes, anger".

He said Philip and Kim's focus was "completely" on their children, with three of their children ill.

Philip was remembered during the Mass as being "funny, loveable, sensible and caring", and as someone who stopped people when going to the local supermarket and around the parish for a chat.

Kim was remembered as being "vocal" and "feisty" and a "most loving, kind and caring person".

"As parents, they adored their children. Their life as a family was a journey of love. And there were many journeys as three of their children faced illness. But through all of that , as a family, completely united and dedicated."

Callum was remembered as having a "mischievous smile" who was "loved by all".

"A dark deed took life from you but your light will shine forever. Because in our hearts, you are a star and you are a winner," the priest told mourners.

Jayden was remembered as a "force of love" whose energy "bounded into the world" when he was born.

articles.title: Search under way for four soldiers missing after gang attack in Haiti
articles.summary: The UN Security Council holds a meeting on Haiti; the attack on UN-backed forces is expected to dominate the discussions.
articles.body:
International forces in Haiti are working to establish contact with four Salvadoran soldiers who went missing after violent gangs attacked their armoured vehicle with explosives on Sunday.

The soldiers from the United Nations-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF) managed to flee the burning vehicle in Croix-des-Bouquets north of the capital, Port-au-Prince.

It is the first major attack on the international force since it began operations earlier this year.

On Monday, the Armed Forces of El Salvador said the soldiers – four aviation technicians – were returning to camp when they came under attack. Helicopters were sent to “establish contact and determine the location of our military personnel”, but they were also fired at as they dispersed personnel.

“Multiple attempts to approach by land and air have been made, but the intensity of the fighting has hampered these,” said the Salvadoran statement.

The GSF said that it is assessing the situation and has advised residents to remain indoors.

The UN Security Council is scheduled to meet later on Monday about Haiti, and the attack is expected to dominate the conversation.

The GSF officially began operations on 1 June but has so far operated only in a limited capacity. A UN statement said it is expected to reach full operational capacity between now and the end of the year.

It currently has more than 1,500 troops on the ground in Haiti, including soldiers from Chad, Jamaica and Guatemala.

No one has claimed responsibility for the attack. It comes as Haiti prepares for its first general election in more than a decade and illustrates the power of armed gangs that control an estimated 70 per cent of the capital, Port-au-Prince.

The area where the armoured vehicle was struck is controlled by gangs, including Kraze Barye, led by Vitelhomme Innocent, and 400 Mawozo, led by Lanmo Sanjou. Both gang leaders have been sanctioned by the UN and US.

“Armed gangs have overrun large parts of Port-au-Prince, the capital, employing tactics including murder, kidnapping, and sexual violence amid widespread impunity,” said a UN Security Council report last month.

Since the assassination of President Jovenel President Jovenel President Jovenel President Jovenel Moise in July 2021, Haiti has been in a multidimensional crisis characterised by extreme violence, political deadlock and dire humanitarian conditions.

Gang violence displaced a record 1.5 million people across Haiti in recent years. The UN says at least 5,700 people have been killed or injured from January to mid-September this year and 230 have been kidnapped.

articles.title: Doncaster Sheffield Airport set to come into public ownership
articles.summary: South Yorkshire Mayoral Combined Authority plans to buy Doncaster Sheffield Airport.
articles.body:
Doncaster Sheffield Airport (DSA) is set to come under public ownership, with politicians on the cusp of agreeing a deal with landowner Peel.

South Yorkshire Mayoral Combined Authority (SYMCA) will buy the airport and adjacent Innovation Quarter employment land - totalling more than 1,000 acres - subject to the deal going through.

It means SYMCA would become the freehold owner and landlord to the City of Doncaster Council lease.

A lengthy report with the financial details will go before senior councillors next week, but SYMCA officers say the "project is not without risk to the taxpayer given the sums of public funding involved".

The proposals are subject to formal approval by the SYMCA board next week and with the agreement of the board of Peel Land.

South Yorkshire Mayor Oliver Coppard said it would be a major milestone in the region's progress towards reopening the airport and to create one of the UK's leading hubs for sustainable aviation, advanced manufacturing and innovation.

The purchase would "provide long-term control, certainty and flexibility", help create thousands of jobs and attract significant private investment, he said.

"This is a deal that puts the future of DSA back in our hands and finally gives one of the biggest and best growth opportunities in South Yorkshire the platform for the long-term success that it needs and deserves."

Coppard continued: "After months of negotiations and the growing flexibility afforded to us by the government's devolution agenda, we have come to an agreement for SYMCA to buy the airport and employment land from Peel.

"Subject to the agreement of the SYMCA board, the airport and surrounding employment land will be owned and controlled by us, for us; the people of South Yorkshire. This deal means our future will be in our own hands again."

The airport closed in November 2022 and since then, City of Doncaster Council has been working to reopen it with public funds after attempts to find a private operator were unsuccessful.

Originally Peel Land was going to lease the site but, over the last 12 months, negotiations have continued to explore options.

There has been devolution of powers and funding to the mayor, and Peel was able to reconsider an option that "was not commercially acceptable" to them in 2022, an SYMCA report said.

Stephen Wild, managing director of Peel Land, said: "There has been significant collaboration and we continue to work closely with our partners at the council and SYMCA to achieve the wider vision."

Buying the airport from Peel would mean local authorities would own both DSA and Fly Doncaster Ltd, the arm's-length company set up by City of Doncaster Council to run the airport.

In September 2025, SYMCA conditionally agreed to provide an additional £160m of funding to support the South Yorkshire Airport City project.

Freight services are planned to return from autumn 2027, with passenger services returning in spring 2028, subject to the regulatory and operational work required to reopen the airport.

The Mayor of Doncaster Ros Jones said to have the airport in public ownership was "the right option".

"This is ambitious and the partnership with SYMCA builds on the strong foundations we have built up over the past four years.

"We have worked hard to get airspace certification and airfield readiness, getting key staff in place and importantly keeping those critical conversations with airlines, businesses and support services going."

Reform UK have the majority of councillors on City of Doncaster Council and were approached for comment.

Dan Fell, chief executive of Doncaster Chamber of Commerce, said the deal would bring certainty for decades to come.

"The region gets hold of the airport for the fullness of time and that's got to be a shrewd and sensible move," he said.

"It opens up different types of conversations and relationships with airlines and carriers, and with potential private sector investors.

"It signals the scale of the ambition for our region. It ensures our regional partners and the politicians have got real skin in the game to make this airport a success."

South Yorkshire leaders will consider the proposals at the SYMCA board meeting on 27 October.

articles.title: Meet Caden Chau, the 17-year-old Calgary student who started with a $50 second-hand 3D printer; his team has now built over 600 assistive devices, while its free designs have reached 400,000 people worldwide
articles.summary: A Calgary teenager who started a youth-led project to improve accessibility with a second-hand 3D printer bought for $50 has been named one of Canada's
articles.body: A Calgary teenager who started a youth-led project to improve accessibility with a second-hand 3D printer bought for $50 has been named one of Canada's top young changemakers of 2026. Caden Chau, a 17-year-old high school student, founded MakeAble to create custom, affordable assistive devices for people with physical disabilities and neurodivergent conditions. Over the past three years, the organisation has grown from his home in Calgary to reach people in Toronto and Vancouver. In recognition of his work, Children First Canada named Chau the winner of the Health for All Award for Health Equity at the third annual Future is NOW! Awards, held at the Fairmont Royal York in Toronto. The award recognises Canadians under 18 who develop practical solutions to major health and social problems.Scaling up custom assistive devicesMakeAble began when Chau bought a used 3D printer for $50 and started experimenting with digital design files. Working directly with occupational therapists and local community partners, Chau and his volunteer team have designed, printed, and distributed more than 600 custom assistive devices. These include hundreds of special sensory toys created with Alberta Children's Hospital. The toys help neurodivergent children feel more comfortable during medical treatments and therapy sessions. To make sure its designs reach people beyond western Canada, MakeAble offers a free online library of more than 30 original assistive device designs that anyone can access and use. According to award details published by Children First Canada, these downloadable designs have been accessed and used by more than 400,000 people worldwide. The project's growth has also attracted financial support from national disability organisations. This includes a $9,000 growth grant from the Neil Squire Society.Expanding equity in peer support and musicAlongside his work with assistive technology, Chau has started several community programmes in Alberta to help people overcome social and academic barriers. After noticing that some classmates struggled to find study help they could access, Chau started Peer Tutoring Services at his high school. He recruited and trained more than 30 volunteer tutors, who provided hundreds of hours of free academic support. Surveys of participants found that 85 per cent faced fewer barriers to getting academic help, while 95 per cent reported lower levels of school-related anxiety. Chau also serves as an executive officer with the Art2Heart Society, a non-profit organisation that provides thousands of music lessons across more than 10 countries. As part of his volunteer work, Chau has personally taught more than 300 one-to-one piano lessons designed for students with learning disabilities.National recognition and launchpad fundingAt the Future is NOW! Awards ceremony in Toronto, Sara Austin, founder and CEO of Children First Canada, spoke about the importance of supporting young people who develop practical solutions to real-world problems. “These young people aren't waiting for the future to arrive; they are already building it,” Austin said in a press statement released by Children First Canada. “At a time when children are facing enormous challenges, these 10 young changemakers are responding with courage, creativity and commitment. Today, we're not simply giving them an award; we're giving them a national launchpad and investing in everything they can become.” As part of the recognition, each recipient received $1,000 in seed funding for their project. They also received a year of formal mentorship, leadership coaching, and networking opportunities organised through Children First Canada. Before accepting his award on stage, Chau joined 40 other young advocates from across Canada at the Future is NOW! Youth Summit. The event was an immersive leadership conference designed to connect teenage entrepreneurs with mentors from business, government, and civil society. Chau continues to manage MakeAble while completing high school. He is focused on adding new open-source designs to the project's online library and building partnerships with more hospitals across Canada.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Brazilian court orders Meta to prove Lula and Bolsonaro get equal treatment
articles.summary: A judge also doubled the daily fine for noncompliance with a previous court order governing political content.
articles.body:
Brazil’s top electoral court has doubled a daily fine for the United States-based social media company Meta, saying it failed to comply with an order about how political content is shown on its platforms.

On Monday, the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) gave Meta 24 hours to show that it is not favouring one presidential candidate over the other in its content feeds.

The decision comes less than a week before Brazilians vote in a presidential run-off that pits left-wing incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva against right-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro.

“The continued noncompliance, just a few days before the run-off election, demonstrates that the fine imposed was insufficient,” a TSE judge said in Monday’s order.

The penalty for noncompliance was also increased in the order, from 500,000 Brazilian reals ($100,000) to one million reals ($200,000).

The court order is in response to a complaint from Lula’s campaign that Meta prevented his profile from being fully promoted on Instagram and from being visible in searches.

His campaign has also argued that posts by Lula’s supporters are being disproportionately taken down by moderators, who are instead allowing content promoting his rival or questioning the integrity of elections.

Civil society groups and digital rights monitors have supported those allegations, saying Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp — three platforms run by Meta — have suppressed content from the left-leaning leader while boosting posts promoting Bolsonaro.

Meta has denied favouring either candidate on its platforms, although it admits some of Lula’s campaign ads were taken offline temporarily due to technical errors.

Lula and Bolsonaro are set to face off in a final round of voting on Sunday. Bolsonaro, the son of an imprisoned former president, performed better than many analysts expected in the first round of voting on October 4.

He garnered 47 percent of the vote, compared with Lula’s 45 percent. Neither, however, crossed the 50-percent threshold needed to avoid a run-off. Pre-election polling puts the two virtually neck-and-neck going into Sunday’s vote.

Social media bias has been a point of contention on both sides of Brazil’s political sphere.

Earlier this month, Lula’s campaign launched a website to document complaints from supporters about their activities being unfairly restricted on Meta and other social media platforms.

Several digital rights groups, such as the nonprofit CTRL+Z, have published findings that suggest Meta may have helped Bolsonaro have an outsized presence on its platforms, which many in Brazil use as their main source of news.

“Brazilian citizens have the right to know why their accounts were banned, why their posts disappeared, why their accounts lost reach, and why they are being prevented from commenting, reposting, and saving content,” CTRL+Z wrote on its website.

“Meta cannot be the invisible judge of the Brazilian electoral debate.”

On Friday, the Brazilian newspaper Folha de S Paulo reported it had reviewed internal messages between Meta employees acknowledging they were aware of the inconsistent treatment of Lula and Bolsonaro’s social media presence.

Political campaigns in Brazil have dramatically increased their spending on social media platforms like Facebook and Instagram, outpacing traditional avenues like television or street advertising in recent elections, said Daniela da Silva, the executive director of CTRL+Z.

According to data collected by the Supreme Electoral Court, Facebook received more than 200 million reals ($40m) in revenue in the 2024 municipal elections, ranking at the top of advertising suppliers for that cycle.

Despite that revenue, da Silva said that Meta and other companies were not taking their responsibility towards election fairness seriously.

“These are very powerful, wealthy companies, and they do have the capacity to do much more than they are doing,” she told Al Jazeera.

More than 100 civil society groups, including Greenpeace International, Global Witness and Oxfam Brazil, have joined CTRL+Z to sign a letter calling on Brazilian authorities to enforce rules meant to rein in Meta.

They have also pushed the company itself to do a better job removing deepfakes and disinformation, and to provide clear rules on how it moderates content.

“We want transparency regarding moderation criteria, a human review channel, and timely responses to protect the election,” the group said on its website.

articles.title: In 2018, an Indiana father set up a trust to keep his second wife in a retirement home costing $4,000 a month; his children said it harmed their inheritance, but an October 14 court barred their lawsuit as too late
articles.summary: An appeals court in Indiana has dismissed a legal malpractice lawsuit filed by two siblings against an estate planning lawyer.
articles.body: An appeals court in Indiana has dismissed a legal malpractice lawsuit filed by two siblings against an estate planning lawyer. The court ruled that their challenge over their late father's $3 million (£2.3 million) trust was filed after the legal deadline. In a decision issued on October 14, 2026, a three-judge panel of the Court of Appeals of Indiana upheld a trial court ruling in favour of Columbus attorney F. Jefferson Crump III. The trial court had granted summary judgment, meaning the case was decided without a full trial. The lawsuit was filed by Julia Beaman and William Bobbs Jr. They claimed that Crump failed to meet his professional duties when he prepared an irrevocable trust in 2018 for their father, William Bobbs Sr. The trust was meant to pay for the care of his second wife at a retirement community that cost about $4,000 (£3,070) a month. Writing for the unanimous appeals panel, Judge Patricia A. May ruled that the siblings' claims were too late under Indiana's two-year deadline for filing legal malpractice lawsuits.Creation of the estate plan and retirement trustAccording to court filings published by Justia Law, William Bobbs Sr. married his second wife, Carolyn Janice "Jan" Bobbs, in 1999, after his first wife died. In August 2017, the couple met with Crump to create an estate plan. They wanted to make sure Jan could continue living at the Four Seasons Retirement Center in Columbus, Indiana, if her husband died before her. In January 2018, Bobbs Sr. signed a Qualified Terminable Interest Property (QTIP) trust agreement. It placed about $3 million in assets under the care of First Financial Bank, which acted as the custodian. Under the agreement, Bobbs Sr. had the right to receive income from the trust while he was alive. After his death, the trustee had to pay Jan all the net income from the trust, along with any money from the main fund needed to cover her monthly fees at the Four Seasons community. Those fees initially stood at about $4,000 a month. The agreement also stated that any money and assets left in the trust after Jan's death would go to Bobbs Sr.'s two adult children, Beaman and Bobbs Jr.Siblings challenge trust terms and attorney conductBobbs Sr. died in May 2020. After his death, Jan suffered a fall and had to be moved to an intensive care unit at the retirement facility. As the cost of her care rose sharply, First Financial Bank approved larger monthly payments from the trust to cover her expenses. In February 2022, Beaman and Bobbs Jr. filed a lawsuit against Crump and Jan in Marion Superior Court. They argued that the irrevocable trust allowed more money to be paid to Jan than their father had intended, reducing the inheritance they would eventually receive. The siblings accused Crump of negligence, helping to enable undue influence, and failing to meet his professional duty of care. They also claimed that Bobbs Sr. did not have the mental ability to sign an irrevocable trust in January 2018. They argued that Crump had a conflict of interest because he had represented Jan in the past. To support their claims, the siblings submitted a transcript of a secretly recorded family lunch in December 2017. During the meal, Bobbs Sr. incorrectly told his children that the trust could be changed or cancelled and that he could take the money back at any time. Court records showed that Bobbs Jr. also told his father during the lunch that he suspected Crump had a conflict of interest. He said he had discussed his concerns with lawyers he knew.Court applies two-year limitation periodCrump asked the court to grant summary judgment, arguing that the siblings had filed their legal malpractice lawsuit too late. Under Indiana Code section 34-11-2-4, legal malpractice claims must be filed within two years of the date the claim begins. Under Indiana's discovery rule, the two-year period starts when a person knows, or should have known through reasonable care, that they have suffered harm because of an attorney's alleged wrongful act. The Court of Appeals of Indiana found that the siblings knew the facts behind their claims as early as December 2017. At that time, they discussed the trust with their father and raised concerns about Crump's role in preparing it."Plaintiffs were aware of their alleged injury no later than January 10, 2018, when Bobbs Sr. executed the QTIP Trust Agreement," Judge May wrote in the official opinion. "Because Plaintiffs did not file their complaint until February 24, 2022, more than four years later, their claim is barred by the two-year statute of limitations." The appeals court added that even if the deadline had been paused while Bobbs Sr. was alive, the siblings still filed their lawsuit more than two years after he signed the trust documents and they first learned about its terms. Judges Rudolph R. Pyle III and Paul D. Felix agreed with Judge May's opinion. Their decision left the trial court's ruling in favour of the estate planning lawyer unchanged. Jan Bobbs died in September 2023 while the case was still ongoing. Her estate was later named as a co-defendant before the appeals court issued its final ruling.You use AI every day. articles.title: Rare photos of Myanmar’s ex-leader Aung San Suu Kyi show her receiving books sent by King Charles
articles.summary: Myanmar’s military-backed government said Monday that it had delivered two books sent by King Charles III to detained former leader Aung San Suu Kyi, along with a sealed envelope and diplomatic correspondence.
articles.body: BANGKOK — Myanmar’s military-backed government said Monday that it had delivered two books sent by King Charles III to detained former leader Aung San Suu Kyi, along with a sealed envelope and diplomatic correspondence. President Min Aung Hlaing, who seized power in February 2021 as an army chief, has been seeking to end Myanmar’s international isolation, imposed after Suu Kyi was ousted and imprisoned. Min Aung Hlaing has faced sanctions but is now trying to project a return to normalcy after holding an election in 2025 and increasing Myanmar’s engagement with its regional neighbors. The Presidential Press and Information Bureau said in a statement released on its Telegram channel that two officials from the Home Affairs ministry delivered the materials to Suu Kyi in the capital, Naypyitaw, that morning. The books were identified as The Land Gardeners: Soil to Table, by British authors Bridget Elworthy and Henrietta Courtauld, which explores the relationship between healthy soil and food, and Soil: The World at Our Feet, the catalog from an environmental exhibition in London. Charles, who has long championed environmental protection and sustainable agriculture, met Suu Kyi in London in 2017, when he was Prince of Wales and she was Myanmar’s state counselor. Suu Kyi, who has served several sentences in prison and under house arrest, has spoken about the influence of literature on her life during her previous periods of detention, and is known to enjoy fiction and detective books. Accompanying Monday’s statement were two photos of the 81-year-old leader dressed in a traditional pale green blouse and skirt and seated across a small table from two men in white shirts inside a wood-paneled room. The statement did not provide details about the correspondence nor explain how the books were sent. The meeting lasted about 10 minutes, according to the statement, which did not disclose the location nor provide details about what was discussed. The announcement provides another rare update about Suu Kyi’s circumstances while she remains in detention. She is currently serving her sentence under house arrest at an undisclosed location in Naypyitaw on charges that her supporters and rights groups have said are politically motivated. She has not been seen publicly since then and her whereabouts and condition have been largely kept from public view. In August, a representative of the International Committee of the Red Cross visited Suu Kyi, her first known contact with an outside international independent humanitarian organization since her detention in February 2021. International community, including Myanmar’s fellow members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, has called for Suu Kyi’s release and access to or engagement with Suu Kyi as part of efforts to resolve the country’s political crisis but the government has rejected the calls.

articles.title: The rioting across France is a symptom of a much larger public and political crisis
articles.summary: “We have a mess on our hands, to put it bluntly,” French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said Monday.
articles.body: “We have a mess on our hands, to put it bluntly,” French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said Monday. If anything, he might be guilty of understatement. After widespread rioting at the weekend – estimated to have cost several hundred million dollars in property damage and theft – France faces a toxic mix of urban rebellion, political drift and economic crisis. The disorder at the weekend occurred in major cities across the country, leading Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez to offer his resignation because of the police’s failure to contain the rioting. There was rampant looting in Paris, Marseille, Bordeaux and other cities, while the city hall in Limoges, which survived two world wars, was badly damaged by fire and its clock spire collapsed. The violence at the weekend, which led to some 2,400 arrests, followed weeks of protests by French students angry about crumbling schools, a lack of teachers and dismal job prospects. More than 6,000 arrests were made during the school protests that began at the start of the fall term and more than 100 schools were damaged. More demonstrations are scheduled for next weekend. In November, labor unions plan to strike. France faces a winter of discontent in the run-up to a presidential election next spring. The far-right candidate Marine Le Pen is leading in the polls. Political drift In a national televised address Sunday, President Emmanuel Macron condemned the violence but did not set out ideas to deal with it or seize the initiative. Instead, he warned of politicians seizing on the chaos for political gain – before leaving France for a three-day visit to the Gulf states. Lecornu similarly deployed the blame game. After far-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon accused the government of “opening the door to chaos” with its policing tactics, Lecornu shot back: “You cannot call for an end to the violence while providing excuses to those who commit it. This is YOUR political responsibility.” Le Pen, who is standing in the presidential election for the far-right National Rally party, has sought to inject the issue of migration into the debate, blaming the violence on delinquents from France’s banlieues, poor urban areas where much of the country’s migrant population lives. “Our country is caught in a vice…between violence and powerlessness,” she said, suggesting only her firm hand could restore order amid Macron’s “chaos.” The president of her National Rally party, Jordan Bardella, poured fuel on the fire, demanding that “Antifa militias, far-left extremist groups and Black Bloc groups” be designated as terrorist organisations.” Black Bloc groups wear matching or similar black clothing along with face masks during protests to hide their identity. Analysts say this political fragmentation, which led to the paralysis of parliament after snap elections called by Macron in 2024 backfired, is likely to persist – and is at the core of France’s deepening crisis. The political center in France has evaporated, allowing the National Rally and Mélenchon’s far-left France Unbowed party to harvest growing public exasperation, while Macron’s successive prime ministers have been unable to pass a budget through Parliament. The multitude of candidates in the center, “most with relatively few supporters, will ultimately help secure the second-round election for one of the two contenders who represent the greatest danger to democracy in France,” wrote Robert Zaretsky, a professor of modern French history at the University of Houston, in an essay for the Atlantic. Debt and déclinisme The current crisis has polarized an already deeply divided society. Besides the shock and anger at the weekend’s mayhem, there is an air of defeatism. In a recent Ipsos-BVA poll, 85% of respondents said that France was in decline, and 98% were dissatisfied with the present state of the country. Whoever governs France next will have shrinking room for maneuver, even if they can stitch together a stable coalition. The French economy is stagnating. Farmers were hit by an extremely hot and dry summer, while global energy prices stoked inflation. Tourism remains a strong earner for France, but the videos of violence on the streets circling the globe in the past two days may deter some travelers. French businesses are wary of the drift and indecision. Investment has fallen about 1% in the first half of this year amid climbing interest rates. Above all, there is the debt. “France carries one of the highest government debt burdens in Europe, and political deadlock means we expect its debt level to continue rising,” researchers at Oxford Economics said in July. France will have to issue a record high of €340 billion in medium- and long-term bonds next year, according to analysts. Its debt as a proportion of gross domestic product (GDP) rose to 119% in the second quarter of this year, double the European Union’s target. Jittery investors sent the country’s 10-year government bond yield up to 4.9% on Monday. Its reputation in bond markets is not helped by Mélenchon’s plan to freeze or wipe away the French sovereign bonds held by the Bank of France. “Political fragmentation may persist well after the 2027 elections, meaning that France’s next government will continue to kick the public-finance can down the road,” said Oxford Economics. This would “prolong the existing climate of high uncertainty, weighing on confidence and domestic demand.” The man most revered by the French, General Charles de Gaulle, once declared that “France cannot be France without grandeur.” De Gaulle had soaring ambitions for the country’s global role and independence. But during his long presidency he also told an aide: “I keep the theater going as long as I can and then, after me, have no illusion, things will go back to where they were.” De Gaulle stepped down a year after the 1968 riots that shook France – events that some commentators are likening to today’s shock. When he became president, Macron was seen as the antidote to what the French call déclinisme (a word that first appeared in the French Larousse dictionary in 2016.) “He delivers an extremely positive, constructive message, full of hope for the future. He shows that there is also another France,” wrote one commentator. A decade later, Macron’s approval rating is hovering at about 15 to 17%, according to multiple polls Déclinisme is still very much on the lips of a citizenry that is demanding more from a beleaguered state that has less.

articles.title: Mauritius lifts curfew imposed amid wave of violent protests
articles.summary: Unrest on the archipelago came after police shot a woman during a rally over rising costs and water shortages.
articles.body:
Mauritius has lifted a nighttime curfew that was imposed last week amid a rare wave of violent demonstrations.

The government announced on Monday that the “favourable evolution of the situation” had allowed the end of the curfew. The protests on the Indian Ocean archipelago began last week over water shortages and the rising cost of living, but violence exploded after a police officer shot and seriously wounded a woman on Saturday.

“The curfew currently in effect will not be extended, effective today,” the office of Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam said in a statement.

“The last curfew ended at 4:30am on Monday 19 October, and it has not been extended. Roads are open, all schools have reopened with classes running as usual, and daily life is back on track,” the Mauritius Tours tourism operator confirmed on its website.

The unrest saw at least 188 people arrested on charges including looting, arson, damage to police stations, and possession of explosives in the following days.

The police officer who shot the woman in the neck has been arrested and brought to court, authorities said.

The island nation of Mauritius is usually viewed as a model of stability and prosperity in Africa. The last major unrest was in 1999, when a renowned singer died in police custody.

However, the unrest provoked a British government update of its travel advice, which urged people travelling to the popular holiday destination to take care.

“The Government of Mauritius introduced temporary curfews during the evenings and overnight, covering most areas of the main island, which lasted from 12 October to 18 October, ending at 4.30am on Monday 19 October,” the British government said in a statement.

“Stay away from demonstrations and large public gatherings and follow the advice of local authorities,” it warned tourists.

articles.title: Ukrainians dying because US restricting intelligence sharing, Zelensky adviser tells BBC
articles.summary: Serhii Beskrestnov says there has not been enough time to warn people about incoming missile attacks. The White House said there had been no changes to intelligence sharing.
articles.body:
Ukrainians have died because Kyiv is still not receiving reliable US warnings of incoming Russian attacks, according to a key adviser to President Volodymyr Zelensky.

Serhii "Flash" Beskrestnov told the BBC that lives had been lost because there had not been time to warn citizens about ballistic missile strikes, saying: "It's dangerous... I think it's really very bad... People [have] already died."

The adviser also said restrictions to Ukraine's use of the Starlink internet network were ongoing.

The White House said there had been no changes to intelligence sharing with Ukraine.

Ukraine first reported an interruption to US intelligence sharing last week , as a row with the Trump administrations over its controversial deal to import Russian oil sent relations to new lows.

Despite the denials from Washington, many in Kyiv suspect the issues are not a coincidence.

On Monday morning, Zelensky wrote on social media: "Overnight two ballistic missile attacks were reported on the capital, one without warning, the second with only minimal time to take shelter."

Hours earlier, an interview the president did with NBC was published, in which he said intelligence sharing had been restored after a three-day pause.

"We are very thankful for this," he said. "Only [the] United States has this unique intelligence to tell our side when Russia uses ballistic missiles."

But Beskrestnov told the BBC that American intelligence continued to be incomplete and inconsistent, and that the US had failed to provide a clear explanation for the issue.

"This looks very strange," he said. "Sometimes we receive this information before the attack, another time we [do] not."

He continued: "And for example, last night we received it, but... one minute before the attack."

However, he said other collaboration with US continues, adding: "Intelligence data keeps flowing, and the issue is solely with the air raid alert component."

Beskrestnov also said the US had given no clarity about who was responsible for the ongoing restrictions to the Starlink internet network and its military service Starshield, which Kyiv uses to provide connectivity for drones, helicopters and military communications.

Last week, Starshield restricted the speed at which mobile units could move while staying connected to the network to 100mph (160km/h).

This has limited Ukraine's ability to shoot down incoming drones or to launch mid-range drone attacks into Russian-occupied areas.

Starlink owner Elon Musk said last week that the US government ultimately controls access to Starshield, which was designed for the Pentagon, suggesting it may therefore be behind the restrictions. Trump has denied involvement.

Beskrestnov said he thought both issues occurring at the same time was "probably" a deliberate move to put pressure on Ukraine.

He told BBC News: "It's probably the United States trying to say [to] us, 'let's have the conversation, negotiation with Russia, you should find the compromise'."

Beskrestnov also said Ukraine had its own radar data to provide some limited warning of incoming attacks, but was urgently looking into using alternative communication systems.

He added: "Now we understand that something begins to happen with Starlink, and we're not sure what will be the next step.

"We understand that we should be prepared for some problems in future. And now we're thinking about an alternative for Starlink, not only for air defence, for communication between our forces, between our staff, for civilians also, because we don't know what we should expect in future regarding Starlink."

Earlier on Monday, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there had not been a "pause" to intelligence sharing.

"I don't know where [Zelensky is] getting these things or why he's saying these things to the press," he told reporters on Monday.

Rubio said he could not comment on the incident, adding: "I know a few nights ago there was a software problem involving their early warning system."

The BBC has contacted Starlink for a response.

A White House official said there were no changes to intelligence sharing operations between the US and Ukraine.

The official spoke on background to discuss intelligence matters. Trump is focused on ending the war, the official said, and added that the US has provided more aid to Ukraine than any other country.

articles.title: Trump admin cuts to satellites will set back US weather forecasting by a decade, experts say
articles.summary: The Trump admin reduced the number of planned US weather satellites and removed key tools. Experts say it will set our weather forecasts back nearly a decade.
articles.body: The Trump administration’s cuts to weather satellites will set the country back nearly a decade, experts say. The loss of data used to observe, forecast and research extreme weather could prevent the country from making major advances in weather prediction in the coming years. This finding comes from a new report released Friday from the Government Accountability Office, and a letter sent to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration on Monday from Democratic lawmakers. The GAO report details ramifications from budget cuts made to the program for developing new geostationary weather satellites. These large satellites orbit the Earth at a fixed distance, centered over specific spots on the planet. They take the imagery of swirling clouds and storm systems that people see on the evening news or on their weather app each day. The data gathered by these satellites are crucial to issuing accurate weather forecasts. The budget reductions are aimed at taking the program from $19.6 billion in lifecycle costs to $13 billion. But they introduce the risk of a gap in satellite coverage between when the first of the current geostationary satellites, known as the GOES-R series, reaches the end of its service life, and when the first new satellite comes online in 2032, the GAO found. Any gap in satellite coverage, which the GAO warned could last for several months, would deprive weather forecasters of vital weather observations and could reduce forecast accuracy. CNN has reached out to NOAA for comment. The new satellite program is called the Geostationary Extended Observations program, or GeoXO. Last year, the Trump administration directed NOAA and NASA, which is working with NOAA to develop the spacecraft, to reduce the number of satellites that would be part of the new constellation from six to four, and to eliminate three of the five instruments that these satellites are each slated to carry. As CNN reported last year, the instrument changes were partly motivated by a push to narrow the satellites’ applicability to weather forecasting, rather than conducting climate research as well. Among the instruments that were nixed: a tool to monitor air quality, including hourly monitoring of wildfire smoke; as well as one meant to study water quality and ocean currents, along with harmful algae blooms. But so too was a new version of an instrument carried by GOES-R satellites, known as the Geostationary Lightning Mapper. This sensor, first deployed on a GOES satellite in 2017, can detect lightning flashes anywhere on the globe and has proved to be useful for predicting tornadoes as well as monitoring the rapid intensification of tropical storms and hurricanes. Other applications include weather forecasting for aviation and wildfire monitoring. The first GeoXO satellite will have none of those instruments on board when it launches in 2032, the GAO report stated. Instead, it will carry tools already available on previous satellite models, such as a visible and infrared imager to track storms day and night and an infrared sounder that can be especially useful in feeding data into weather models by taking a vertical snapshot of the atmosphere. The sounder data includes conditions like wind speed and direction as well as humidity levels. Originally, NOAA was planning to have three geostationary satellites operating simultaneously, one over the Eastern US, one above the Central US and another above the West. In addition, NOAA requires a spare satellite to be capable of taking over for one of the operational satellites in case of an instrument failure or other mishap. However, given the new budget cuts and instrument changes, there will now only be a GeoXO satellite over the East and one over the West, along with a backup satellite. The GAO questioned whether these new satellites are more advanced than what is in orbit. “It is unclear whether GeoXO will improve, or even continue, the functionality available in the current generation of satellites,” the report said. The lightning mapper’s absence represents a loss of capabilities from the current generation of GOES-R satellites. “Our need for weather information is much greater now than it was ten years ago,” said Steve Volz, who used to lead NOAA’s satellites division and is now CEO at HyperionEO LLC, a consulting firm focused on Earth observations. He said the other nixed instruments would have specifically addressed “stated requirements from Congress.” He warned the cuts made to instruments on the GeoXO satellites could put the US behind Europe, Japan and China in advancing forecast accuracy. The top Democrat on the House science committee, Zoe Lofgren, and Democratic member Gabe Amo wrote in a Monday letter to the NOAA administrator that the administration is poised to set the US back years on weather forecasting rather than advancing its capabilities. “Thanks to the Trump Administration, the next generation of America’s weather satellites could very well be worse than the current ones,” the letter, shared first with CNN, states. “Two fewer satellites and three fewer scientific instruments are not line items in a budget. They represent a concrete, tangible weakening of America’s ability to understand the weather, the climate, and the world around us,” the letter says. The letter seeks information from NOAA leadership regarding any cost-benefit analyses completed regarding the loss of certain instruments from GeoXO, among other documents.

articles.title: BBC calls France protests 'mostly peaceful' as footage shows rioters torching cars, battling police
articles.summary: BBC News called France riots "mostly peaceful" as its own footage showed burning cars, looted shops and nearly 1,000 officers injured nationwide.
articles.body: BBC "News at Ten" host Jane Hill introduced a Sunday report detailing widespread riots across France, where thousands were arrested and nearly 1,000 law enforcement and emergency personnel were injured, before the network's Paris correspondent described the demonstrations as "mostly peaceful" while footage showed burning cars, looted businesses and violent clashes with police. Hill outlined the scale of the destruction before introducing Paris correspondent James Waterhouse's report on the nationwide unrest. "Across the country, nearly a thousand police officers and firefighters were injured. The Interior Ministry says nearly 2,400 people were arrested," Hill said. FRENCH NEWSPAPER RIPS MACRON AFTER RIOTS ERUPT ACROSS FRANCE: ‘INDELIBLE STAIN’ Despite the figures, Waterhouse characterized the demonstrations as largely peaceful while reporting on the approximately half-million people who gathered across France to protest rising living costs and deteriorating public services. "In Paris and beyond, half a million people had filled cities across France to protest over the future of their country. They were mostly peaceful, but as we saw in the capital, in the wings were those who wanted to take advantage of the disorder," Waterhouse said. The BBC defended its coverage in a statement to Fox News Digital, maintaining that its reporting accurately reflected the scale of the unrest while distinguishing between peaceful demonstrators and those responsible for the violence. "No one watching, reading or listening to BBC News coverage of the France protests and riots can be in any doubt as to what was happening – there is coverage of the fires, the looting and violence," the spokesperson said. "James Waterhouse and the team of reporters in France over the weekend gave broader context to the protests and riots – making the point that as well as the destructive scenes, several hundred thousand people were on the streets in peaceful protest, and those carrying out the violence and looting were a small fraction of that number." WHO'S WHO: INSIDE FRANCE'S 'CHAOS INC' FRANCHISE OF COMMUNIST GROUPS, LABOR UNIONS AND GLOBAL ACTIVISTS The White House responded to Fox News Digital's request for comment on the escalating violence in France, a key U.S. ally, by pointing to two Truth Social posts from President Donald Trump addressing the unrest. In his Sunday post, Trump blamed immigration for the violence and urged French authorities to close the country's borders. "France is burning! The immigration of people from an entirely different world, people with hatred in their hearts, has shattered that once great country," Trump said. The president doubled down on his immigration concerns in a Monday morning post, calling for immediate border restrictions. "The migrants have taken over France. They must CLOSE THE BORDERS, FAST! President DJT." VIOLENT FAR-LEFT RIOTS IN FRANCE ARE 'CHILLING WARNING' FOR AMERICANS AT HOME, MIKE JOHNSON SAYS The BBC's footage showed masked rioters clashing with police, setting vehicles ablaze and ransacking businesses, including a wine shop and an electric bicycle store. Waterhouse acknowledged that the destruction was being attributed to individuals exploiting the larger demonstrations. "The shops that have been hit have been completely gutted. Like this wine shop has been looted from top to bottom," Waterhouse said. French President Emmanuel Macron condemned the violence during a televised national address Sunday, distinguishing between demonstrators with legitimate grievances and those responsible for widespread destruction. "Nothing justifies it, nothing explains it, nothing excuses it. Tonight, we all feel anger and shame," Macron said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE The violence prompted French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez to offer his resignation Monday, which Macron rejected. Nunez acknowledged that police had lost control in several major cities as the government considered additional security. According to a report Monday by Agence France-Presse, more than 2,500 people have been arrested, nearly 1,000 security personnel have been injured and at least 3,000 businesses were affected by the unrest. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu called for localized curfews to restore public order. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Fox News Digital reported that rioters also set fire to the historic Limoges Town Hall, built in 1883, causing extensive damage to the landmark. Waterhouse maintained that the violence was largely the work of individuals exploiting the demonstrations rather than those who had gathered to protest rising living costs and deteriorating public services. "Few believe this was at the hands of the genuine protesters, but down to an opportunistic minority who came in and sought to rob and cause carnage," Waterhouse said.

articles.title: Beauty brands are reformulating their bestsellers without talc — here’s why, according to experts
articles.summary: Regulations on talc in cosmetics have been causing reformulations across beauty products. I spoke to cosmetic chemists and dermatologists about potential safety issues and whether you should shop talc-free.
articles.body: Talc has been in your favorite eyeshadows, setting powders and blushes for decades, but you may have recently spotted the phrase “talc-free” when scanning product labels. Why are popular brands like Charlotte Tilbury, Nars and Laura Mercier moving away from the ingredient that has long served a functional purpose in cosmetics, and does choosing a talc-free product actually matter? I spoke to cosmetic chemists and board-certified dermatologists about the concerns surrounding talc, plus everything you should know when shopping for makeup. I also rounded up some talc-free products that brands have recently reformulated or always had in their lineup. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. What is talc’s purpose in cosmetics? Talc typically functions as a texture ingredient in powder-based color cosmetics like eyeshadows, powders and blushes. It helps powders feel smooth, blend evenly and resist caking, and it may help absorb oil and reduce shine, says Dr. Alexandra Bowles, a board-certified dermatologist at MONA Dermatology. Talc is also generally well tolerated by most skin types and isn’t a common cause of allergic reactions, experts say. “When someone does react to a powder, fragrance, preservatives or other ingredients in the formula are often more likely to be responsible,” says Bowles. The appeal of talc is that it’s incredibly versatile and multifunctional, says Esther Olu, a cosmetic chemist and licensed esthetician. “It’s also relatively inexpensive, widely available and compatible with a variety of other cosmetic ingredients,” she says. That includes pigments (it can even help distribute them and increase color payoff, says Olu), dry powders and binders like silica. While talc as an ingredient tends to be gentle on the skin, the concern usually lies in sourcing and testing. What does the current scientific evidence say about the safety of talc in cosmetics? The science is generally mixed. In 2019, FDA testing found trace amounts of asbestos in nine talc-containing cosmetic products, including Johnson & Johnson’s talc-based baby powder and some cosmetic products sold at Claire’s, which were voluntarily recalled. A wave of lawsuits over asbestos-contaminated talc followed. In 2024, the WHO’s cancer agency classified talc as “probably carcinogenic,” citing limited but consistent evidence for ovarian cancer. But at the same time, recent FDA testing of cosmetic samples has repeatedly come back negative for asbestos. When people talk about talc and safety, dose and application is an important piece of context that’s usually missing from the conversation. “The ovarian-cancer data comes largely from women using loose powder in the genital area daily for decades, which is a world apart from pressed powder on your eyelids. Headlines rarely make that distinction,” says Dr. Gina Maccarone, a triple board-certified cosmetic surgeon and founder of The Surgeonista. The “probable carcinogen” classification can also be easy to misread. “It describes whether something may be capable of causing cancer under certain conditions, not how likely it is at everyday levels of exposure,” says Bowles. Many people seem to assume talc and asbestos are interchangeable, but they’re distinct minerals that can occur together in nature. “Talc on its own isn’t considered toxic, but contamination can happen when it’s mined near asbestos deposits,” says Bowles. “As a result, where the talc comes from and how it’s tested may matter more than whether it appears on the label.” It can help to think about the ingredient and the supply chain separately. Contamination has been documented, but it’s relatively uncommon, experts say. “I usually suggest looking for brands that share where their talc comes from and whether it undergoes independent asbestos testing,” says Bowles. In late 2024, the FDA proposed a new rule requiring manufacturers to test talc-containing cosmetics for asbestos contamination. A year later, the FDA withdrew that proposal due to legal and testing complexities. So why are beauty brands going talc-free? Regulation and consumer concern both appear to be driving the change. The European Union is moving toward banning talc in cosmetics in 2027, and many brands may be reformulating globally rather than making separate versions. “The underlying worry tends to be about contamination rather than talc itself, since talc is mined and can occur near asbestos deposits. I think of the shift as a response to trust and regulation rather than a sign that talc is harming the skin,” says Bowles. However, “brands aren’t waiting for the science to fully settle,” says Maccarone. “Reformulating to talc-free is cheaper than the reputational and legal risk, so brands are getting ahead of it.” Reformulation based on changing regulations isn’t new in the beauty world. In fact, changing formulas have been one of the biggest trends in beauty this year (my favorite Skinceuticals C E Ferulic Serum being one of them). For example, Neutrogena rolled out a new, reformulated Hydro Boost line in Europe and North America without cyclic silicones (like cyclopentasiloxane and cyclomethicone) ahead of EU bans due to environmental concerns. Similarly, bestsellers like the Armani Beauty Luminous Silk Foundation, Charlotte Tilbury Magic Cream and Bobbi Brown Cosmetics Vitamin Enriched Face Base all reformulated this year to comply with silicone regulations. “When a major market changes its regulations, global brands must decide whether to reformulate products across their entire portfolio or maintain different formulations for different markets,” says cosmetic chemist Ava Perkins. Top talc-free makeup Instead of reformulating its bestselling Airbrush Flawless Finish Pressed Powder, Charlotte Tilbury launched a new, talc-free loose setting powder in August. The brand sent me the powder to test ahead of its launch, and I still use it months later. It blurs, brightens and controls oil, and as someone who has used the original pressed powder for years, I find it is equally as good at keeping my makeup from creasing and reducing shine throughout the day. Loose powders also apply much better on my dry skin than pressed powders, which can be a little too heavy and cakey, especially under my eyes (although the loose powder is slightly messier to use with my powder puff). It comes in six shades to accommodate various skin tones, too. Charlotte Tilbury released the Airbrush Flawless Blush Blur at the same time as its loose powder, which is also talc-free and has phenomenal color payoff while still looking natural, in my experience. Mac Cosmetics reformulated its popular Studio Fix Powder, a two-in-one foundation and setting powder, in 2025 to be entirely talc-free after more than 30 years on the shelf. The reformulation was met with shock and outrage by loyal fans, who claim texture, coverage, finish and longevity were vastly different from the original. But with more than 70 shades, the powder foundation is one of the most shade-inclusive talc-free options on the market. It also has a matte finish and all-day oil control, even without talc, according to the brand. The popularity of Nars’ powder blushes dates back decades. I remember buying the bestselling Orgasm shade after seeing it in almost every beauty YouTuber’s videos before being an “influencer” was ever really a thing (though the shade was far too pink for me, it was still a status symbol to even have it). The brand reformulated its blush line without talc in 2024, and with it came some strong changes, including a sleeker, refillable compact (rather than the classic, matte rubber packaging), a vegan formula and eight additional shades. To replace talc, Nars added a blend of synthetic and natural mica and kaolin clay, which gives it a silkier texture and blurring effect, according to the brand. Givenchy’s Prisme Libre was one of the first loose powders I ever tried, and it’s the reason I generally prefer them over a pressed powder. As someone with noticeable dark circles, I’m a big fan of the color-correcting shades, which I combine to create the perfect illuminating, shadow-reducing finish. Givenchy reformulated its Prisme Libre powder without talc in August 2024, replacing it with kaolin (white clay) and synthetic mica. Although I haven’t tried the original (now discontinued) formula, the current powder is extremely light, easy to blend and doesn’t have a cakey finish. Similar to Charlotte Tilbury, Huda Beauty did not reformulate its popular Easy Bake Blurring Loose Baking & Setting Powder without talc (and recently launched a talc-containing Brightening + Correcting Duo Loose Powder), but it did release a new talc-free pressed powder. As a longtime fan of the brand’s loose powder, I tried the pressed powder at the time of its launch and was very impressed. It’s much more lightweight and less heavy or cakey than I expected, which is a huge plus as someone with dry skin. It completely blurred my pores and reduced any shine or oily that may have come up on hot days outside. It’s also noncomedogenic, which means it won’t clog pores and cause breakouts on my acne-prone skin. All of Saie’s products are talc-free, so it comes as no surprise that the brand’s new SuperSuede Baked Eyeshadow, which launched in August 2026, doesn’t have any traces of it, either. The newest Bellini shade, which is a rose gold with peachy-pink undertones, was released this month in partnership with beauty and lifestyle creator Hannah Chody after her favorite Tom Ford eyeshadow shade was discontinued. It has a suede-like finish that doesn’t crease, fade or flake off. It also has a subtle shine that’s not too flashy, which means you can wear it on its own or with a full face of makeup. Kosas specifically notes in its site that it follows the EU’s clean standards, banning over 2,700 ingredients that might irritate skin, disrupt hormones or cause harm to the environment, including talc. This pressed powder is a favorite of NBC Selected editorial operations associate Jem Alabi, who uses the Candy shade. “It’s a sheer pink that brightens my under eyes while also giving me a flush that looks natural throughout the day,” she says. “A little goes a long way with this one and I love that it works for any skin tone. You can even use it by itself to control shine.” However, many reviewers note flaws with the packaging, saying it’s bulky and breaks easily. Older, discontinued Patrick Ta products did have talc, but the brand has largely shifted away from the ingredient in recent launches (with the exception of the Major Skin Crème Foundation and Finishing Powder Duo, which still contains talc). Patrick Ta’s latest releases, the three new Major Dimension Eyeshadow Palettes, are all talc-free and have hyaluronic acid and squalane for a soft texture and smooth application. Plus, the packaging is stunning, so I store it proudly on top of my vanity. Should you throw out your talc-containing cosmetics? It’s a personal choice, but all of my experts agree: Don’t panic-buy talc-free products. “It’s a reasonable, low-cost choice if it gives you peace of mind, and good talc-free alternatives exist. But tossing every product in a frenzy isn’t warranted by the evidence,” says Maccarone. Pressed powders, blushes and eyeshadows from reputable brands tend to carry a low risk, says Bowles. You can also check whether a brand shares its asbestos-testing practices to help guide your decision. If you do want to replace your talc-containing products, start with loose powders and any body powders, then replace other products gradually as they run out or expire, says Bowles. Keep in mind that the importance of the “talc-free” label in the beauty industry is heavily influenced by marketing and consumer perception, experts say. The label itself tends to have an underlying meaning. “It’s the implication that a product is inherently safer simply because it doesn’t contain talc,” says Olu. “Brands understand that consumers are increasingly paying attention to ingredient lists, and removing controversial ingredients can become a way to differentiate products in a competitive market.” However, products containing talc are not automatically unsafe, says Olu. We also take steps to ensure all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and without undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. Dr. Alexandra Bowles is a board-certified dermatologist at MONA Dermatology in Cincinnati, Ohio.Esther Olu is a cosmetic chemist, licensed esthetician and instructor.Dr. Gina Maccarone is a triple board-certified cosmetic surgeon and founder of The Surgeonista in Cincinnati, Ohio.Ava Perkins is a cosmetic chemist, PhD student researcher and content creator, Why trust NBC Selected? I’m a commerce editor at NBC Selected who has written about beauty and skin care for more than six years. I’ve also spent years testing new beauty products on the market. For this article, I spoke to board-certified dermatologists and cosmetic chemists about the potential risks of using talc-containing cosmetics, what the science says and whether you should look for talc-free alternatives. I also gathered some talc-free beauty products I’ve tested and loved, as well as favorites from NBC Selected staffers. articles.title: An Ohio customer pulled a one-of-one Shohei Ohtani and Aaron Judge baseball card from a $2025 Topps Chrome pack; it later sold for $2.16 million
articles.summary: A baseball card found in a pack of cards in 2025 has sold for $2.16 million at auction.
articles.body: A baseball card found in a pack of cards in 2025 has sold for $2.16 million at auction. The rare card features Shohei Ohtani and Aaron Judge, two of Major League Baseball’s biggest stars, and includes gold Logoman patches and both players’ autographs. A customer at All-Pro Sportscards in Cuyahoga Falls, Ohio, discovered the card last summer in a pack of 2025 Topps Chrome.According to Baseball America, the card later went up for auction through Fanatics Collect, where it attracted 52 bids. It eventually sold for $2.16 million, including a $360,000 seller’s fee on top of the $1.8 million winning bid. The identities of the buyer and seller have not been made public.How did the Shohei Ohtani and Aaron Judge card sell for $2.16 millionThe card sold on Fanatics Collect in an auction that was scheduled to end late on Thursday, but continued into the early hours of Friday. Its final price was $2.16 million after 52 bids. That total comprises a $1.8 million hammer price and a $360,000 seller’s fee.The card had already reached $190,000 within three minutes of being listed on March 5. The buyer and seller have not been publicly identified. Topps posted that the card had been pulled by a customer at All-Pro Sportscards in Cuyahoga Falls, Ohio, during the previous summer.The one-of-one card features game-worn gold Logoman patches and two autographsThe one-of-one card is part of the 2025 Topps Chrome collection and features gold Logoman patches and autographs from both players. Each patch comes from a jersey worn during a game in which the player hit a home run. Ohtani’s patch was taken from a jersey he wore on May 26 against the Cleveland Guardians.Judge’s patch came from a game four days later, when he faced Ohtani and the Los Angeles Dodgers. The gold Logoman design was introduced by Major League Baseball and Topps for the 2025 season. Six players, including Judge and Ohtani, wore the gold patches that year, each representing a reigning award winner in Major League Baseball.How MLB award winners shaped Topps’ gold Logoman cards in 2025 and 2026The gold Logoman design was introduced for the 2025 season and appeared on the jerseys of six players who held major MLB awards. Ohtani and Judge wore the patches as the reigning Most Valuable Players (MVPs). The other players were reigning Cy Young Award winners Chris Sale and Tarik Skubal, and reigning Rookies of the Year Paul Skenes and Luis Gil.Topps used patches from all six players in cards across several releases during the year. Ohtani and Judge repeated as MVPs in 2025, so both were set to wear gold Logoman patches again in 2026. Skubal and Skenes were also returning as reigning Cy Young winners, while Nick Kurtz and Drake Baldwin joined as the 2025 Rookies of the Year.Other cards have fetched higher pricesThe dual Ohtani-Judge card sold for less than Ohtani’s solo Gold Logoman card, which fetched $3 million at auction in December 2025.One week before the dual card sold, Judge’s 2013 Bowman Draft Superfractor autograph sold privately for $5.2 million, a modern-card sales record. The dual Gold Logoman’s price was also below a record-setting basketball card sale: a dual NBA Logoman autograph featuring Michael Jordan and Kobe Bryant sold for nearly $13 million in 2025.You use AI every day. articles.title: MP seeks tighter checks on drug supplies from neighbouring states
articles.summary: MP Malvinder Singh Kang orders strict monitoring of drug supplies from neighbouring states, inspections and action against illegal sale of habit-forming medicines in Punjab.
articles.body: Patiala: Sri Anandpur Sahib MP Malvinder Singh Kang on Sunday directed officials to tighten monitoring of medicine supplies from neighbouring states and crack down on the illegal sale of habit-forming and restricted drugs in Punjab.Chairing a meeting at the District Administrative Complex in Ropar, Kang ordered stringent action against medical stores violating regulations and called for closer surveillance of outlets in villages and towns.Officials reviewed enforcement in Ropar, Shaheed Bhagat Singh Nagar, Hoshiarpur and SAS Nagar districts, including inspections, medicine seizures, cases registered and action against drug licences over the past two to three years. Pending cases, repeat offenders, illegal supply networks and the performance of drug control officers were also discussed.Kang said the state govt had taken several measures to curb illegal sales, but concerns persisted over medicines entering Punjab from neighbouring states and being sold outside authorised channels.He called for regular inspections, greater accountability and action to identify sources of illegal sales and dismantle supply chains. Pending cases should be disposed of promptly in accordance with law, he added.Kang also sought a time-bound action plan for the entire Sri Anandpur Sahib parliamentary constituency, with clear targets, regular reviews and measurable progress. He stressed interdepartmental coordination and continuous monitoring to curb the illegal sale of narcotic and habit-forming medicines.Drug inspectors from the four districts were directed to submit detailed reports on enforcement measures taken and planned. articles.title: Two wanted in antique dealer kidnap case arrested; carried Rs 25,000 reward
articles.summary: Lucknow police arrested two ₹25,000-reward suspects in an antique dealer kidnapping-extortion case; ₹1.34 lakh recovered, gang posed as cops to steal ₹13 lakh.
articles.body: Lucknow: Police on Monday arrested two wanted men carrying rewards of ₹25,000 each in connection with the abduction and extortion of an antique dealer who was allegedly kidnapped by a gang impersonating police officers and forced to hand over ₹13 lakh in cash along with gold and silver jewellery. Police said ₹1.34 lakh in cash was recovered from the two during the operation.The arrests were made by a joint team of Krishna Nagar police and the Southern Zone Surveillance Cell as part of an investigation into what police described as an interstate network involved in kidnapping and extortion.The accused were identified as Pankaj Bhushan Kumar (47), a native of Nalanda district in Bihar currently living in Hyderabad, and Navneet Singh (32), a resident of New Behsa in Lucknow’s Sarojini Nagar area. DCP South Zone Mohammed Mustaq said the duo had been absconding since the case was registered at Krishna Nagar police station.Police said six other accused linked to the case were arrested on Sept 20 and sent to judicial custody. Investigators tracked the remaining suspects using CCTV footage, technical surveillance and local intelligence inputs, Mustaq said.According to police, the case relates to the alleged kidnapping of Sudarshan Ghosh, an antique dealer who lives in the Alambagh area. Investigators said the gang targeted him after collecting information about his business and financial condition.ADCP Vasant Kumar Rallapalli said interrogation indicated the group identified people believed to have substantial wealth. Police alleged Navneet, who had prior links with the antique trade, knew Ghosh and tipped off other members about valuables the dealer possessed. The suspects then conducted reconnaissance of Ghosh’s movements before allegedly executing the crime on Sept 12.Police said several gang members approached Ghosh near his office, introduced themselves as police personnel, displayed forged identity cards and forced him into a vehicle under the pretext of official questioning. The kidnappers allegedly threatened him and made him call his family to arrange money for his release.Investigators said Ghosh’s driver later delivered ₹13 lakh in cash and gold and silver ornaments to the gang, after which the victim was released near Shaheed Path. articles.title: ‘Requirement not arbitrary’: HC upholds Hry eligibility test for PG trained teachers
articles.summary: Punjab and Haryana High Court upholds Haryana rule making HTET/STET mandatory for PGT appointments/promotions, rejecting challenges as non-arbitrary.
articles.body: Chandigarh: Punjab and Haryana high court has held that persons appointed or promoted as Post Graduate Trained Teachers (PGTs) in Haryana must compulsorily pass the Haryana Teachers Eligibility Test (HTET)/School Teachers Eligibility Test (STET).A division bench of Justice Harsimran Singh Sethi and Justice Minderjeet Yadav dismissed a bunch of writ petitions filed by Kuldeep Singh and others, challenging the Haryana State Education School Cadre (Group-B) Service Rules, 2012, which prescribe HTET/STET as a compulsory qualification for appointment to PGT posts in the state.“...in totality, the qualification which has been prescribed under 2012 Rules so as to hold/possess the qualification of HTET/STET in order to become eligible, cannot be treated as arbitrary, illegal or without jurisdiction...” the bench held in its recent order.The petitions challenged the requirement of HTET/STET, particularly in the context of advertisement no. 4 dated June 28, 2015.The petitioners argued that the National Council for Teacher Education’s (NCTE) Nov 12, 2014, notification prescribing qualifications for Classes 11 and 12 teachers did not include HTET/STET. They contended that the state govt’s additional requirement was contrary to the NCTE notification and that Centre-prescribed qualifications would prevail in case of a conflict.On this, the court referred to Supreme Court’s judgment in Preeti Srivastava versus state of Madhya Pradesh (1999) and observed that the qualifications prescribed by the Union constituted minimum requirements and that the state could prescribe higher qualifications to improve teaching standards, provided the minimum qualifications were not diluted.Opposing the petitions, the state through additional advocate general Sanjiv Kaushik submitted that under the Right to Education Act, 2009, HTET/STET was compulsory for Trained Graduate Teachers (TGTs), who formed the feeder cadre for promotion to PGT posts. It argued that the qualification was necessary for the promoted cadre as well.The state counsel further submitted that PGTs also teach students of Classes 7 and 8 and relied on Supreme Court’s judgment in Anjuman Ishaat E Taleem Trust versus state of Maharashtra, contending that Supreme Court had held that the eligibility test was mandatory for teachers teaching students up to Class 8.The court further observed that, under the 2012 Rules, PGT posts were filled through direct recruitment and promotion from the TGT cadre. Since HTET/STET was an essential qualification for appointment as a TGT, prescribing it for the higher post of PGT, including through direct recruitment, could not be considered arbitrary.
